words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.tr: adj. 时代错误的；落伍的；过时的
words.ex: Wearing a horse-drawn carriage in modern times is anachronistic.
words.ex_cn: 在现代穿马车是过时的。
words.en: Something that is anachronistic is out of its proper time in history, or seems to belong to a different time.

words.ex: He gave an antagonistic reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了敌对的答复。
words.en: If someone is antagonistic to someone or something, they show hatred or opposition towards them.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；莽撞的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a brusque answer and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with or say things quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

words.ex: The cacophonous noise made her cover her ears.
words.ex_cn: 刺耳的噪音让她捂住了耳朵。
words.en: If you describe a mixture of sounds as cacophonous, you mean that they are loud and unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.tr: adj. 吵闹的；喧哗的；吵吵嚷嚷的
words.ex: The clamorous crowd cheered loudly for the winner.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群为获胜者大声欢呼。
words.en: If you describe people or their voices as clamorous, you mean they are talking loudly or shouting.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.tr: adj. 居高临下的v. 屈尊；俯就；表现出优越感；“condescend”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a condescending smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了一副屈尊俯就的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is condescending, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they talk or behave in a way which shows that they think they are superior to other people.

words.tr: adj. 深感懊悔的；痛悔的；悔悟的
words.ex: He felt contrite after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr: adj. 符合礼仪的；得体的；高雅的
words.ex: She behaved in a decorous way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上举止得体。
words.en: If you say that something is decorous, you mean that it is dignified, proper, and socially acceptable.

words.ex: He was deferential to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师很恭敬。
words.en: If you are deferential, you are polite and respectful towards someone, especially because they have a higher position or status than you.
